transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

Well… I’m probably making more of it than I should, but I’ve been a bit unsettled at school. I’m a secondary school teacher, and lately I keep feeling like certain staff emails or even the morning announcements are… sort of coded messages about me. 

My colleagues have been kind and they’ll point out, “No, this was sent to everyone,” and I do understand that, but I can’t quite shake the feeling. I thought maybe it would be best to talk to someone, just to check I’m not overreacting.
Do you feel like these messages are being directed at you on purpose, or that someone is trying to communicate something specific to you through these emails or announcements?

I suppose… yes, a little. I don’t mean I think everyone’s sitting around plotting or anything like that. It’s more that when certain staff emails come through, or the morning announcements are read, I get this strong feeling that there’s something in them about me, like a message tucked inside.

And I know my colleagues have shown me they were sent to everyone, and I do understand that logically. I don’t want to sound difficult. It’s just… the feeling doesn’t really go away.

Do you often feel that things people say or things that happen around you—like something on the radio, a TV show, or even people talking in the hallway—are directed at you personally or contain hidden messages meant for you?

Yes… I suppose that’s what I’m worried about, really. Not so much television or radio, but at school, with certain staff emails or the morning announcements, I get this feeling that they’re somehow about me, like there’s a coded message in them.

I do know that sounds a bit odd, and my colleagues have been very kind about showing me they were sent to everyone. I understand that part. I just… I can’t quite shake the feeling, and I don’t want to make a fuss if it’s nothing.
Have you noticed this same feeling of hidden messages or things being directed at you outside of school, like in public places, on social media, or through news broadcasts?

Not really, no… at least, I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed it so much in public places or on the news or social media.

It’s mainly at school — certain staff emails, and sometimes the morning announcements. I know they’re sent or said to everyone, and people have kindly shown me that, so I do understand. It’s just that I still get this feeling they’re somehow about me, like there’s something tucked into them. I hope that makes sense… I’m not trying to make it sound bigger than it is.

Outside of school, do you ever feel that random things people say or do—like strangers talking in a café or something written in a newspaper—are directed at you or contain hidden meanings meant for you?

No, not really… I don’t think I’ve had that feeling outside of school. If I’m in a café or reading a newspaper, I don’t usually think it’s aimed at me.

It’s more the school things that unsettle me — certain staff emails, or the morning announcements. I know they’re for everyone, and people have gently shown me that, so I do understand that part. I just can’t quite shake the feeling that there’s something coded in them about me. I’m sorry, I know that may sound strange.
Are these feelings of hidden messages limited only to the school setting, or have you noticed similar experiences happening in other areas of your life, even occasionally?

I think it’s really only at school, yes. I haven’t noticed it in other parts of my life, not in the same way.

It’s just those staff emails and the morning announcements that… well, I get this feeling they’re somehow coded messages about me, even though my colleagues have shown me they go to everyone. I do understand that, honestly. I just can’t quite shake the feeling, which is why I thought I should come in and ask about it.
Have you ever had any other unusual beliefs or suspicions that others around you don’t seem to share, even if they seem very real to you?

I don’t think there’s anything else, really… not that I can think of. It’s mainly just this one thing at school.

I came in because I can’t quite shake the feeling that certain staff emails and the morning announcements are… well, sort of coded messages about me. Even when my colleagues very kindly show me they were sent to everyone, I do understand that. I don’t want to sound difficult or dramatic. It just still feels real to me sometimes, and that worries me a bit.
Have you ever had any beliefs or suspicions that others around you don’t seem to share, even when they seem very real to you, outside of these experiences at school?

Outside of school? No… I don’t think so. Not really.

It’s more that one situation I mentioned — the staff emails and morning announcements. I know they’re sent to everyone, and people have been very kind about showing me that, so I do understand it logically. I just… I can’t quite shake the feeling that there’s something in them about me, like a coded message.

But outside of that, I can’t think of anything similar. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Have you ever, even in the past, had any beliefs that others didn’t share—something that felt very real to you but others saw differently—outside of what you’ve described happening at school?

No, I don’t think so… at least, nothing outside of school that I can remember.

It really is just this one thing with the staff emails and the morning announcements. I know I’ve mentioned it a few times — I’m sorry if I’m repeating myself — but that’s the only belief like that I can think of. It just feels as if they’re coded messages about me, even though people have shown me they go to everyone. I do understand that part. I just can’t quite shake the feeling.
Have you ever had any other unusual or strong beliefs that turned out not to be true, even if they seemed very real to you at the time?

Only the school thing, really. I’m sorry, I know I keep coming back to it.

At the time it does feel very real — like certain staff emails or the morning announcements are somehow coded messages about me. But then my colleagues will gently show me they went to everyone, and I can see that, logically. So… I suppose that’s the main belief that might not be true, even though it feels quite convincing when it’s happening.

Have you ever had any experiences, even in the past, where you strongly believed something that others didn’t agree with — something that turned out not to be true — even outside of these school-related feelings you’ve described?

No… not really outside of the school situation. I hope that makes sense — I’m not trying to avoid the question.

The only thing I can think of is what brought me in, really: I get this feeling that certain staff emails or the morning announcements are somehow coded messages about me. And I know, when colleagues show me they’ve gone to everyone, I can see that logically. It’s just… the feeling doesn’t quite go away.

But apart from that, I don’t think I’ve had other beliefs like that.
Have you ever had any other fixed, false beliefs that persisted despite clear evidence to the contrary, even if they seemed very real to you at the time?

I think… yes, in the sense of the school messages, but I don’t want to overstate it.

It’s not that I have lots of beliefs like that. It’s really just this one thing I came in about — I can’t seem to shake the feeling that certain staff emails, and sometimes the morning announcements, are somehow coded messages about me. Even when my colleagues very kindly show me that they were sent to everyone, I can see that with my rational mind… but the feeling still sort of stays there.

I know that probably sounds odd. I’m trying to answer properly. Apart from that, I don’t think there’s anything else.
